subject: Business Models
title: Healthcare Subscriptions
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Healthcare Subscriptions.

hook.text: One Medical charges $199/year for same-day appointments and 24/7 virtual care. Amazon bought them.

buildup.text: Direct primary care practices charge $50-200/month. No insurance claims, no waiting rooms, longer visits.

discovery.text: Subscription healthcare removes the per-visit fee, encouraging patients to come earlier and prevent disease.

twist.text: Critics say subscription healthcare creates a two-tier system: premium for subscribers, long waits for everyone else.

climax.text: Amazon's acquisition of One Medical signals that tech giants see subscription healthcare as the future.

punchline.text: Pay $199/year, skip the waiting room. Healthcare is subscribing too.

quiz.question: What's the main benefit of subscription healthcare for patients?
options: Removing per-visit fees encourages preventive care

details.summary: Healthcare subscriptions provide ongoing medical services for monthly fees, from telehealth consultations and mental health therapy to prescription delivery and preventive care monitoring. Companies like One Medical, Hims, and Noom are making healthcare access a recurring subscription product.
details.whyItMatters: Healthcare subscriptions are addressing access gaps in traditional insurance-based systems by offering transparent pricing and convenient delivery..
takeaways: Monthly fees provide ongoing access to medical services and prescriptions
Telehealth and digital-first models reduce delivery costs significantly
Subscription healthcare addresses price transparency and access concerns

faq.question: What types of healthcare services work best as subscriptions?
faq.answer: Primary care memberships with same-day virtual and in-person visits, mental health therapy with regular sessions, chronic condition management with ongoing monitoring, prescription delivery services, and preventive wellness programs all translate naturally into subscription models.

faq.question: Can healthcare subscriptions coexist with traditional insurance?
faq.answer: Yes, most complement rather than replace insurance. One Medical charges a membership fee for enhanced primary care while still billing insurance for services. Subscription models work alongside insurance to fill gaps in access, convenience, and preventive care that insurance does not cover.
